text:
acme_billing: Hey team — our invoice creation started returning 422 / structured output parse errors since ~12:10 UTC yesterday. We didn't change any client code except upgrading the SDK. Example request we send:

acme_billing: ```json
{
  "invoice_id": "12345",
  "amount": "1500",
  "paid": "yes",
  "status": "PAID"
}
```

acme_billing: Response from Redwood API: ```json
{
  "error": "structured_output_parse_error",
  "details": ["field \"amount\": expected number, got string", "field \"paid\": expected boolean, got string", "field \"status\": enum case mismatch (expected lower-case)"]
}
```

jane.support: Thanks for the repro. Can you paste the request-id/headers from the failing call and the SDK call you ran? Also did you flip any API flags (json_mode/strict) recently?

acme_billing: request-id=rid_0a1b2c3d, SDK v2.4.1, we set `json_mode: "strict"` on the client when upgrading (default used to be lax). Curl we ran:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/invoices \  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-...' \  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \  -d @payload.json
```

matt.engineer: this matches strict-mode behaviour — strict JSON mode does not coerce types or case for enums. Historically many customers relied on coercion, so upgrading SDK and enabling strict is a common trigger.

matt.engineer: quick repro locally: model returns `"amount": "1500"` and our structured parser fails because schema expects number. Also `"paid": "yes"` isn't a boolean.

matt.engineer: Suggested short-term workarounds: 1) set `json_mode: "lax"` on the client to allow coercion, or 2) perform a lightweight transform at your API gateway to coerce numeric strings and common boolean words (`yes/no`, `true/false`) before sending to Redwood.

luis.sre: Looking at our runtime traces for rid_0a1b2c3d — the model generated stringified values. Log extract:

luis.sre: ```
2024-06-12T12:09:58Z [trace rid_0a1b2c3d] model-output: {
  "invoice_id": "12345",
  "amount": "1500",
  "paid": "yes",
  "status": "PAID"
}
parser: strict schema validation failed: amount type mismatch; paid type mismatch; status enum case mismatch
```

jane.support: Thanks — that confirms model output is the source (not a transport corruption). Please confirm whether you enabled `strict` intentionally; if so we should either relax parsing or add documented guidance.

acme_billing: We didn't realize strict would flip on with the SDK upgrade — we enabled it to catch schema regressions. We want to keep strict but need a reliable way to avoid these failures.

matt.engineer: Understood. For medium-term fix we can: A) make our parser accept numeric strings that parse as numbers when `strict:true` if the string is unambiguous, and B) accept common boolean tokens (`yes/no`, `y/n`, `true/false`) mapping to true/false for boolean fields. Also normalize enum casing (case-insensitive match preferred with warning). We'll need eng-runtime to sign off on policy because strict was intended to be strict.

jane.support: I'm escalating to eng-runtime. Matt — can you open an internal ticket with reproducible snippet, logs (rid), and suggested patch? Add regression tests and a feature flag so we can roll out conservatively.

matt.engineer: Created ticket R-4578. Attached repro, logs, and a proposed hotfix: allow numeric-string coercion + boolean-token mapping under a compatibility flag `allow_coerce_unambiguous=true` even when `json_mode: "strict"`. Patch linked in ticket.

luis.sre: While eng evaluates, I pushed a temporary API-gateway transform rule for Acme (rid=0a1b2c3d) that coerces numeric strings to numbers and maps `"yes"/"no"` to booleans for their tenant only. Deployed at 12:45 UTC. deploy-bot: https://deploys.redwood.ai/runs/7890 (gateway-rule: acme-coerce-7890)

deploy-bot: Deployment successful: gateway transform applied to tenant acme_billing (rule acme-coerce-7890) 

luis.sre: Monitoring now shows failing 422 rate drop to zero for Acme over the last 15m. Backend logs show parser still strict but model outputs are transformed before validation.

acme_billing: Confirmed — errors stopped. Appreciate the quick mitigation. Are you planning a platform-level change so other customers don't hit this unexpectedly?

jane.support: Yes — eng-runtime will triage R-4578 and decide whether to add the compatibility flag as opt-in or change default parsing behavior with clear release notes. We'll also add a KB article describing how SDK upgrades can flip `json_mode` and what to check in upgrade guides.

matt.engineer: Next steps: add integration tests for numeric-string and boolean-token coercion, add a feature flag gating, and include opt-out tests to ensure strictness remains enforceable. ETA for a staged rollout: 2 weeks pending reviews.

acme_billing: Thanks — for now the gateway rule works. Please keep us updated in the ticket and DM the SRE if anything weird pops up.

jane.support: Closing loop for support channel; keeping R-4578 open. @matt.engineer @luis.sre please update when PR is merged. :thumbsup:
